text:
javier: Heads-up — in ap-southeast1 we've been seeing a burst of tiny gpu pod evictions for the last 20m, looks like a packing/egress interplay. eviction count ~120 in 15m.
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-pod-evictions > 100 in 15m (ap-southeast1). Affected nodes: g3-*-rack3.
chiara: Is this the usual tiny-inference fleet or something new?
matt: Mostly tiny inference (50-100m runtime), lots of pods requesting fractional gpus + strict nodeAffinity to warm-node labels.
olivia: Quick theory: warm-pool warmpods have high egress to our logging/metrics endpoint, hitting node egress limits -> conntrack/cni churn -> scheduler sees pods as failing and evicts.
javier: That matches packet drops on the node logs I peeked at 10m ago. Also seeing many Pending->Killed cycles, scheduler message: "node lost readiness" then eviction.
kevin: Two levers: reduce per-pod egress rate (agent side) or relax affinity so small pods spread more evenly. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
chiara: Can we try a short experiment: 1) taint a tiny warm-pool subset with 'egress-limited=true:NoSchedule' and 2) update pod tolerations to prefer non-egress-limited nodes? If that reduces evictions we confirm egress is the trigger.
matt: Alternative quick fix: bump conntrack / sysctl on the affected nodes via kexec rolling or machine config. But that'll be heavy and might not be allowed in prod during peak.
javier: I can roll a conservative taint now to a single rack and watch. planning window 10m, will report metrics.
infra-bot: Runbook note: check Node.Conntrack.Occupancy + CNI drop counters before/after.
olivia: Add cost note: if we spread tiny pods across more instances to avoid tight packing we'll increase hourly GPU cost ~12-20% depending on binpack.
kevin: For a medium-term fix we should change scheduler scoring to penalize nodes with high egress bandwidth usage for these fractional-gpu pods. That keeps packing but avoids hotspots.
sre-oncall: If you taint, please also add a canary rule in autoprovisioning so we don't spin up new warm nodes that reintroduce the problem.
javier: Taint applied to rack3-warmpool nodes now. Starting 5m observation window.
chiara: Do we have a quick grafana panel link for the conntrack and pod evictions? post it here so we can watch.
javier: grafana: https://grafana.redwood/sys/board/evictions?var-region=ap-southeast1 (watching Live).
kevin: If taint helps we should follow with a small scheduler patch: add egressScore = -alpha * normalized_egress. alpha can be tuned; start with 0.7.
matt: Note: scheduler change will need perf test. In the meantime, consider upping the CNI soft-limit for burst on the warm nodes. Low-risk if we throttle logging egress to batched sends.
chiara: +1 on throttling logs at agent side. That reduces egress and keeps packing. Who owns the agent? @olivia?
olivia: Yep I can add a client-side send buffer and backoff in the agent binary, roll to canary in eu-west then ap-southeast. ETA for canary: 6 hours.
sre-oncall: If evictions spike again during the roll, we may need to temp scale a spare warm pool to take pressure (hourly cost but keeps SLOs). Call me if that goes above threshold.
javier: 15m update: evictions on tainted rack down 70%, global evictions down ~30%. conntrack occupancy also lower. Looks promising.
chiara: Great signal. Next actions: olivia to implement agent backoff, kevin to draft scheduler scoring proposal, matt to investigate CNI soft-limit bump feasibility, and javier to monitor for 12h.
kevin: I'll post a PR draft for the scheduler egress score later today.
matt: I'll run a quick node sysctl test on a dev rack to validate no regressions.
olivia: Starting work on agent backoff now, will ping when canary scheduled.
infra-bot: NOTE: Incident transitioned to "mitigated". Continue monitoring. :tada:
javier: Thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source for updates. If anything resurfaces, @sre-oncall escalate.
